audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate mechanical errors, each repeated across the page. (1) Six fields credit Lillia's stacking movement speed to her passive, Dream-Laden Bough. It belongs to Blooming Blows (Q), whose passive component grants stacking Move Speed on spell hits; Dream-Laden Bough is only the damage-over-time. (2) Two fields call Watch Out! Eep! a dash. Riot's text says it deals damage in a nearby area — there is no dash in it. (3) Four fields say Liandry's is what turns her damage into percent-max-HP. Dream-Laden Bough is already max-Health damage over time by itself.
audit.why: Each error changes what the player does. Believing the speed is on her passive means trying to deny the DOT to slow her, which does nothing. Believing W is a dash means waiting for a gap-close that never comes and missing the real tell — she stepping inside 500. Believing the percent damage arrives with Liandry's means a Cho'Gath happily stacks Feast health before her first item, when the burn already scales with every point of it. The one thing the page never says is the fact that matters most: the edge of Blooming Blows deals true damage, so no amount of MR reads that trade correctly.
audit.corrected: Reattribute the move speed to Blooming Blows, drop the W-dash claim, state that Dream-Laden Bough is natively max-health burn, and add the true-damage edge on Blooming Blows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Cho'Gath Levels 3, 4-5, First item and 2+ items and give Lillia Level 6. The packet chart is the exact inverse on every one of those rows, and so is the prose.
audit.why: 44.95% over 287 games is one of Cho'Gath's worst top matchups, and the page agrees with the packet in words: 'the trading edge stays hers', 'her first item... punishes your HP stacking', 'the 1v1 is hers', and — the one exception — 'Level 6 is your one window'. The chart currently says Cho'Gath wins four stages of a lane he loses at 45%.
audit.corrected: Chart becomes Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Cho'Gath, Lillia, Lillia with ratings 3, 3, 3, 3, 6, 3, 3. Only Level 6 is Cho'Gath's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows is named as the tracked cooldown in a dozen fields with no number. It is 6s at rank 1 — never a window. Lilting Lullaby, the ability the mid paragraph correctly says the whole mid game hinges on, is given no cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby is 150/130/110 seconds and reaches 1600 units, and it only puts targets to sleep if they already carry Dream Dust from one of her spells. That gating is the actionable fact: if she has not hit you with a skill, there is no sleep to fear. Swirlseed is 12s flat at 700 range and Watch Out! Eep! is 14s at rank 1 at 500 range.
audit.corrected: Retarget focus and cooldowns onto Lilting Lullaby at 150s, and state the Dream Dust prerequisite.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads and the Riftmaker line are right for a lane decided by a 1600-range sleep and sustained magic burn; the page does not over-recommend armour, which would be wrong against a true-damage Q edge and max-health DOT.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lillia is referred to as 'he'/'his' throughout the full layer ('silence his combo', 'if he snowballs', 'half his win condition').
audit.why: Consistent pronouns; the content layer already uses 'she'.
audit.corrected: Fixed in the fields I touched; the remainder is a mechanical sweep.

edits.before: Lillia is the exact kiter your kit hates — her passive (Dream-Laden Bough) grants movement speed when she hits you, and her E (Swirlseed) bounces in to poke from outside your Rupture range, so she never has to stand where your Q lands. Her passive burn out-ticks your Carnivore sustain at levels 1-3, and with no landed Q there's no knockup to chain your Feral Scream silence off. Don't throw a hopeful Rupture she'll just walk out of — last-hit at max range, accept the DOT poke, and wait to punish only when her W (Watch Out! Eep!) dashes her in close.
edits.after: Lillia is the exact kiter your kit hates — Blooming Blows (Q) stacks her movement speed every time a spell of hers lands on you, and Swirlseed (E) rolls in from 700 to poke outside Rupture's landing zone. Dream-Laden Bough burns max health over time, so it out-ticks Carnivore at levels 1-3, and with no landed Q there is no knockup to chain Feral Scream off. Don't throw a hopeful Rupture she walks out of — last-hit at max range, eat the burn, and punish only when Watch Out! Eep! brings her inside 500.

edits.before: This is where she takes over and you can't answer it 1v1. Her Liandry's-fueled passive burn and Swirlseed deal percent of your max HP, so your stacked Feast health melts instead of protecting you, and her R sleep chain-CCs you out of fights while she kites your slow skillshots on passive movement speed. You stay a teamfight asset — Rupture knockup, Feral Scream silence, and Feast peel are real — but don't try to duel her in the side lane. Group with your team and force her to fight inside your CC instead of in open space where her kiting wins.
edits.after: This is where she takes over and you can't answer it 1v1. Dream-Laden Bough burns max health natively and Liandry's only scales it, so your stacked Feast health melts instead of protecting you, and Lilting Lullaby sleeps you out of fights from 1600 while Blooming Blows' stacking speed keeps her off your skillshots. You stay a teamfight asset — Rupture, the silence and Feast peel are all real — but don't duel her in the side lane. Group and force her to fight inside your CC, never in open space.

notes: FLAG MISFIRES, deliberately not written: (1) the kit tags Swirlseed with 'terrain', and _missing/chogath.json therefore says 'Lillia can cut your retreat with Swirlseed'. Riot's description says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target — it creates nothing. I made no terrain claim. (2) Rupture's 'grounding' flag again contradicts Riot's text, so no grounding claim here either. The packet suspectName 'Laden Bough' is a partial-match false positive — the page writes the full 'Dream-Laden Bough' correctly. Level chart: six rows flip in both layers as one atomic group, matching the packet chart and the prose. The full layer refers to Lillia as 'he' in roughly ten fields; I corrected the ones I edited, and the rest is a safe global she/her sweep.
